prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the incretin physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which made possible incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize on B033 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Having read the full first-round exchange and the chair's questions, I find that the scientific case has not weakened under scrutiny. Nobody argues the discovery is immature, and nobody disputes the mechanistic chain: GLP-1 as a gut incretin that potentiates glucose-dependent insulin secretion, identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, receptor biology, and then independent confirmation by large randomized outcome trials in glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal endpoints. I take Svenningsson's point that the evidence does not support waiting for more long-term obesity data; durability data refine the clinical picture but do not alter what was discovered. The citation I now propose deliberately names incretin physiology and the identification of the active form, and does not say first discovery of the incretin concept, which predates these laureates, and does not credit drug development. That wording answers the chair's question about avoiding an implied priority claim while still acknowledging that the physiology enabled the therapies.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the real weakness, and I have not resolved it from the supplied evidence. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested with Habener and colleagues, who are not on the credited list, and with three places there is no trio that is fully fair to everyone who contributed. Excluding Knudsen can be read as a judgement against translation, although I think the discovery-versus-development line is defensible. The prize also gives limited recognition to the early proglucagon and incretin groundwork. If a committee reading of the primary literature were to go against Mojsov, the configuration would be weakened, and I would fall back to Drucker and Holst alone rather than substitute an industrial name.

responses.point: She opened with Knudsen in place of Mojsov, withdrew the substitution in round 1, and says her confidence in the exact trio is lower than in the achievement itself.
responses.response: I think that residual doubt is the honest position and I share it. Where I part from the opening version is that a Knudsen substitution answers an attribution doubt with a different category of credit: the doubt concerns who identified the active peptide, and Knudsen's long-acting analogue chemistry does not bear on that question. If your doubt about Mojsov persists, the principled response is to test the primary record on the peptide, not to swap in a development laureate. I would accept a Drucker and Holst pair as the fallback before I would accept a trio in which the third name rests on a different kind of contribution.

responses.point: He treats B036 (Mori and Walter) as the clean-attribution alternative and notes that a second prize part would force B033 down to two names under the three-person cap.
responses.response: I agree on both points and my view has not moved. B036 is the principal fallback because its credit is clean and the mechanism thoroughly confirmed, but its therapeutic consequence is still prospective, and that gap matters if the choice is between a defensible trio on B033 and a flawless pair on B036. The cap argument also settles the chair's question on a second part: giving B033 only two names to make room for B036 would sacrifice a decisive contributor on the strongest candidate, so I treat B033 as a single-part prize. I do not see an argument that the B036 pair should wait in the same way as B047; it is a candidate for a year in which B033 cannot be awarded cleanly, or for a later one.

responses.point: He observes that Mojsov versus Habener cannot be verified from the supplied text, and offers B036 and B013 as alternatives if attribution is judged unsettled.
responses.response: I agree the supplied text cannot settle priority, and I would not claim otherwise. What I can judge is the structure of the claim: Mojsov's contribution as credited is identification and synthesis of the active truncated peptide, a discrete experimental step that Holst's physiology and Drucker's receptor and proglucagon work build on, and that does not require her to have been first to every observation. Where I differ is on B013 as the fallback. Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer is an earlier, separable line and Eshhar's receptor concept is uncredited, so the CAR-T trio has its own attribution problem. I would rather fall back to B036 than to a configuration whose credit is equally contested.

responses.point: He asks whether a second distinct achievement such as B047 or B011 could be added within the three-person cap without weakening the GLP-1 credit.
responses.response: I considered it seriously, since B047 is a strong mechanism-to-drug story. My conclusion is that it cannot be added without weakening B033. Two parts with at most three names in total means B033 at two names and B047 at one, or the reverse, and each split removes someone with a decisive claim. For B011 the split would be worse, because the channelrhodopsin discovery and the neuronal deployment are separable and both would be underrepresented. I therefore keep a single part, and I would revisit B047 in a later year when the field is more mature and the credit settled.

responses.point: As chair he stresses that the Mojsov question is not settled by the evidence, that Knudsen could be an unfair omission, and that the evidence does not support waiting.
responses.response: I agree on timing. On Knudsen, I hold that the line between discovery and development is principled but I acknowledge it is not free of cost. Her work is decisive for the drugs but is the optimisation of a mechanism already understood, and the physiology laureates did not have that mechanism available to them. A public citation that speaks of discoveries of physiology and the identification of the active form states the boundary openly, without disparaging the later work. I also accept your caution about the central actions of these agents: they are suggestive for neuroscience, but I would not let still-unproven signals in appetite circuits or neurodegeneration carry any weight in the citation.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's claim to the active GLP-1 peptide survives a reading of the primary literature against Habener and colleagues; if it does not, I would reduce the prize to Drucker and Holst.
Whether the discovery-versus-development line, which excludes Knudsen, will be read as principled or as a bias against translation.
Whether a trio of Drucker, Holst and Mojsov fairly reflects the earlier incretin and proglucagon groundwork that is outside the credited list.
How the still-accumulating long-term safety and durability evidence for the newest agents should be reflected, if at all, in the timing judgement.
statement.conflict_note: Updated: no specific conflict with any credited name on the shortlist. My documented connections to Grillner, Ernfors and Perlmann (including one 2009 paper with Perlmann on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons) concern neuroscience work and involve no shortlisted candidate. I use optogenetic methods in circuit work, which is a methodological familiarity with B011, not a personal tie, and B011 is only an alternative in my configuration. I do not see grounds for recusal.
